topic: Mastering the Wordle Opening: An Algorithmic Deep Dive
target_audience: University students and puzzle enthusiasts with a basic interest in logic and data science.

sections.title: The Objective: Shrinking the Search Space
lecture_lines: Wordle is about narrowing down the word pool.
Poor guesses like FUZZY eliminate very few words.
Efficient guesses like TRACE prune the search space quickly.
animations: A dense cloud of 2,315 small white (#FFFFFF) dots fills the screen to represent the word pool.
The word 'FUZZY' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fuzz.svg] appears in grey (#787C7E) boxes; only a tiny fraction of dots vanish.
The word 'TRACE' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/trace.svg] appears in grey (#787C7E) boxes; a massive portion of dots vanish instantly.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Understanding Entropy and Information Theory
lecture_lines: Entropy measures how much uncertainty we reduce.
Information gain splits our pool of possible answers.
One bit of information cuts the possibilities in half.
animations: A single white (#FFFFFF) root node [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/words.svg] appears, labeled 'Total Words'.
The node branches into a binary tree with two levels, showing splitting of possibilities.
One specific path highlights in blue (#5865F2) to represent one bit of information.

sections.title: The Math: The 243 Possible Feedback Patterns
lecture_lines: Each Wordle guess returns a specific color pattern.
There are three possible colors for five positions.
This creates two hundred forty-three unique feedback patterns.
A histogram reveals how words map to these patterns.
Optimal words distribute answers evenly across all buckets.
animations: Show a blank 5-letter Wordle row with white (#FFFFFF) outlines.
Display 3 color squares: Grey (#787C7E), Yellow (#C9B458), and Green (#6AAA64).
The equation '3^5 = 243' appears in bold white (#FFFFFF) at the center.
A histogram with 243 thin white (#FFFFFF) bars appears along the bottom.
The word 'SALET' appears, and dots distribute across the histogram bars evenly.

sections.title: Calculating Expected Information Gain (EIG)
lecture_lines: We calculate expected information using the entropy formula.
Our goal is to maximize the average bits gained.
The word CRANE offers high mathematical surprise.
Bit-Bot computes the average utility of this guess.
A high bit score indicates an excellent opening word.
animations: The Shannon Entropy formula $H = \sum p \cdot \log_2(1/p)$ appears in white (#FFFFFF).
A small green (#00FF00) square 'Bit-Bot' character [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] slides onto the screen.
The word 'CRANE' appears with five color pattern probability percentages floating nearby.
'Bit-Bot' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] pulses yellow (#C9B458) as it calculates the sum of the probabilities.
A final value '5.87 Bits' appears in a large, glowing white (#FFFFFF) font.

sections.title: The Clash of Titans: ADIEU vs. CRANE vs. SALET
lecture_lines: Many players prioritize finding vowels with ADIEU.
However, consonants prune the word list more effectively.
SALET and CRANE outperform ADIEU in average steps.
animations: A list appears with words 'ADIEU', 'CRANE', and 'SALET' in white (#FFFFFF).
Horizontal bars next to each word show remaining possibilities: ADIEU (long), SALET (very short).
The list reorders into a leaderboard [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/leaderboard.svg] with average steps: 1st SALET, 2nd CRANE, 3rd ADIEU in gold (#D4AF37).

sections.title: Practical Application: Your 5-Minute Strategy
lecture_lines: Prioritize high-frequency consonants and avoid repeating letters.
Use top-tier openers like SLATE, CRANE, or TRACE.
Focus on gaining information to solve the puzzle faster.
animations: Icons for high-frequency consonants and a 'no-repeat' sign appear in white (#FFFFFF) and red (#FF0000).
A golden (#D4AF37) 'Cheat Sheet' box appears listing SLATE, CRANE, and TRACE.
A white (#FFFFFF) magnifying glass icon zooms into the final 'Solved' Wordle grid.
